text:
Josh Anderson's season stopped on Nov. 14. He and Mike Matheson are out multiple weeks (reported by the Fresno Bee among others), and the Montreal conversation since has been about what's missing: Sportsnet wrote that the Canadiens must replace his energy, and Habs Eyes on the Prize called it an energy gap. In the same week, Montreal Hockey Fanatics reported Kent Hughes could soon announce a contract extension.

He was scoring when he went down: 8 goals and 12 points in 19 games, all at even strength, on 14 minutes a night. Our numbers flag that pace as due to cool. He was shooting 23% against 16% last season, and Montreal had scored about seven goals more than its chances with him on the ice. The chances themselves were real, though: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.2 scoring chances per 60 from in front of the net last season, 81st percentile.

The flip side is defensive. The Canadiens got about 45% of the expected goals in his five-on-five minutes, and Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last year. Watch how he looks when he returns, because the finishing likely won't come back with him.
